page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m2.6xlarge is a virtual compute instance powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 24 dedicated vCPUs from the AMD EPYC processor family running at a base clock frequency of 2.25 GHz, this instance combines multi-threaded processing power with 48.0 GB of system memory. Operating with a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per core, the configuration emphasizes computational density over deep memory footprints.

The hardware configuration excludes integrated local disks, relying entirely on network-attached block storage architectures for persistent volumes and root systems. Network operations are supported by a baseline throughput capacity of 7 Gbps, facilitating steady data transfer across distributed resources, though public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary with the instance. Hardware graphics accelerators are absent, meaning workloads requiring graphical or tensor computations must run on host CPU instructions.

Positioned with a low memory-per-core ratio, the ecs.u2a-c1m2.6xlarge offers resource density that helps avoid paying for excess, unutilized RAM in compute-intensive environments. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of ephemeral high-speed local storage and restricted memory per thread, which precludes very large in-memory caches. This server type fits parallel processing, batch computing, application build and CI/CD pipelines, web servers, and distributed computing tasks that align with a 1:2 processor-to-memory allocation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m2.6xlarge is an x86_64 virtual instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor, featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs from the AMD EPYC family clocked at 2.25 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio, it supplies 48.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), prioritizing compute resource allocation over large memory pools. The instance includes no onboard local storage, depending on external cloud storage volumes, and does not feature GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Network connectivity offers a baseline throughput of 7 Gbps. This hardware setup minimizes overhead costs associated with excess memory capacity, making it technically suitable for scale-out parallel workloads, continuous integration and delivery runners, batch processing, and microservice architectures that require substantial core counts without demanding extensive memory capacity per thread.
